thread:
Maya Bhat: Quick heads-up — noticed tail latency regressions after we flipped multi-variant routing yesterday. Batches are fragmenting.
Samir Patel: Can you paste profiler outputs? short numbers are fine.
Maya Bhat: From the perf sampler (summary):
```
qps: 1.2k
median_batch: 6 -> 3
p95: 210ms -> 365ms
kv_miss: 7.9% -> 23.4%
compat_frag_rate: +20%
```

Ravi Chen: That kv miss jump aligns with requests landing on different variants so KV keys don't line up. Are variants differing by quant/kernels?
Maya Bhat: Yes — two common variants: same weights but int8 vs fp16. Router favours cheaper int8, then falls back to fp16. So routing creates mixed batches.
Cheng Li: If batches mix quant paths we get kernel-switch overhead + non-shared KV. Could try a queue policy that groups by compatset first. e.g., sticky compat window ~150-250ms.
Samir Patel: I tested locally: increased token_budget_target from 32 -> 48 and toggled compat-priority. Quick result: median batch up to ~5, p95 down to ~240ms, kv_miss down to ~12%. CPU/GPU efficiency drops slightly.
Maya Bhat: Nice. Any profiling on kernel switch cost? Even a few ms per batch could matter.
Ravi Chen: Micro-profile shows kernel_select overhead when the runtime loads a variant-specific kernel path: ~8-12ms on first occurrence, subsequent tokens faster. Exec rates: fp16 ~1.6ms/token, int8 ~1.05ms/token. So mixing hurts due to upfront cost + cache fragmentation.
Cheng Li: Proposed immediate actions:
- short-term: deploy compat-first queue with 150ms sticky window + token_budget_target=48 to Canary A
- mid-term: router-side compat hashing bin by (model, quant, kernel_profile)
- long-term: explore KV normalization so different quant variants can reuse prefix caches when tokenizer+shard match
Samir Patel: Rolling to canary pool A (2 hosts) now. I'll emit per-compatset metrics: batch_size, kv_miss, kernel_swap_count.
deploy-bot: maya requested: canary deploy queued: compat-first-queue v0.1 -> pool-A. Status: queued.
Samir Patel: Canary deployed manually -> metrics streaming. Early: avg_batch on hot routes 3.1 -> 4.6, kv_miss 23% -> 14%. p95 fell ~110ms on those routes.
Maya Bhat: Great. Watch unit cost — raising token_budget increases token churn. We need p95 SLO and unit cost tradeoff analysis.
Ravi Chen: I'll add a kernel swap tracer and a small pre-warm routine for fallback paths to amortize kernel_select.
Cheng Li: Also propose a sibling-first fallback flag: instead of falling to cheapest variant globally, prefer same-compat siblings, then cost order. Make it opt-in for rollout.
Maya Bhat: Agree. Samir, extend canary by 6 hours if metrics hold, then scale to 10%.
Samir Patel: Will do. Posting follow-up traces once kernel-swap data is in.
Ravi Chen: Uploaded kernel-swap trace to the perf bucket (link: s3://perf/1865439876/kernel-swap.json). Early note: pre-warm shaved ~7ms off first-time kernel_select.
Cheng Li: I'll draft RFC for compat hashing + sibling-first fallback tomorrow morning. Target: decision in 48h.
Maya Bhat: Thanks team. If canary is green at 6h we'll proceed. :thumbsup:
